:::{#exm-proof-by-cases}
#### The square of a real number is nonnegative

Claim: for every [real number](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $x$, $x^2 \ge 0$.

Every real number $x$ satisfies $x \ge 0$ or $x < 0$,
so these two cases cover every $x$.

**Case 1: $x \ge 0$.**
Then $x^2 = x \cd x$ is a product of two nonnegative numbers, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so $x^2 \ge 0$.

**Case 2: $x < 0$.**
Then $-x > 0$, and

$$
\ba
x^2
&= x \cd x
&& \text{(definition of } x^2 \text{)}
\\&= (-x) \cd (-x)
&& \text{(the two minus signs cancel)}
\ea
$$

is a product of two positive numbers,
so $x^2 > 0$, and in particular $x^2 \ge 0$.

The claim holds in both cases,
so it holds for every real number $x$.

:::
